packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
Packet 18 - blind image reading (unverified)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. Beyond the rules: I cropped, enlarged and rotated packet images with PIL, including rotating the overview 90 degrees to read the sideways script. I opened no other files.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
The overview (image-001) shows the corner of a book board: a red/pink-edged binding at top and right, with sewing or tie remnants. Three distinct written layers are visible:
 (A) A small parchment corner piece curling up from the board. It carries about 10-11 lines of very small, heavily abbreviated brown-ink script, possibly a late textualis/cursiva in a small module, with many suspension and superscript marks. The lines run diagonally because the piece is curled; they are cut by its torn left and bottom edges and run into the curl at right. There is a red touch (a red stroke or paraph) at the start of line 9. There may be faint ruling lines between lines 2/3 and 8/9. Pink staining is present. The native tile image-002 covers this piece.
 (B) Under it, a paper or parchment pastedown/leaf with LARGE brown cursive running perpendicular to the board edge: about 14 lines are visible in the overview, sideways. When rotated, they read as a list-like sequence of short phrases ending in "-ibus". There is no native tile of this layer; I read it from the reduced overview, rotated.
 (C) On the bare board/pastedown surface at the upper right, later pen trials or scribbles in grey-black ink (loops, "Ego(?)", flourishes). I did not read these as text.
 There is also a printed or engraved double-ruled label frame at the bottom (empty in view), a clear plastic strip at the left, and wormholes.
- Tentative interpretation: (A) looks like a scholastic or logical text ("analogice", "maior/minor", "terminis"). (B) looks like a series of nouns paired with "a [plural noun]-ibus". These are interpretations only.

SELECTED SPANS
I read all visible lines of (A) and the readable lines of (B). Unread: the pen scribbles (C), the top-left marginal fragment of (B), and anything hidden under the curl.

TRANSCRIPTION

(A) Curled parchment piece, image-002 (line numbers from the top of image-002; lines slope down to the right)
image-002 l.1: tu(?) [.]ꝛ(?) . c(?)io(?) [..]
image-002 l.2: e(st)(?) g(?)ꝰ(?)n̄ d(?)[..]ꝯ(?)[..]     [could be "est gen(us)? n(on)"; uncertain]
image-002 l.3: d(?)ar(?) ꝛ analogi(ce)     ["analog-" with an abbreviation at the end is clear; the first word could be "dar/dat/d(icitu)r"; "ꝛ" may be "et"]
image-002 l.4: d(?)eab(us)(?) [.] c(?)ntab(?)ꝫ(?) d(?)ꝫ(?) [..]     [uncertain]
image-002 l.5: s(?)ꝰ(?) . Ex(?) aꝯ(?) h(?) m(aio)r(?) ꝙ(?)[..]     ["m" with superscript "a"/"o" is a recurring abbreviation; could be maior/minor/materia]
image-002 l.6: ena(?)/eu(?)ā m(aio)rem(?)/m(in)orem(?) p(ro)ba(?)t(?)os(?) [..]     [the word after the "m" abbreviation ends in "-n"; "pbatos/pbaros" is uncertain]
image-002 l.7: s(?)e(?) ad v(?)ō(?) [..]cꝫ(?) [..]ꝫ(?) ꝗ(?)e(?) m(aio)r(?) [..]
image-002 l.8: v(?)ba(?) . [red stroke] Itē(?)/Itā(?) ꝛ dn̄(?) e(?)u(?)ē(?) ꝗ(?)r(?) ꝯ(?) [..]     [the red stroke stands before this word; "Item" is uncertain]
image-002 l.9: oīa(?)/om(n)is(?) ꝗ(?) t(er)c(i)a(?)/t(er)m(inus)(?) ꝫ(?) [..] [..]     [could be "q(uod) t(er)cia ..."; uncertain]
image-002 l.10 (lower right on the curl): ... m(aio)r(?) ꝯ(?)' T(?)ermiab(us)(?)/t(er)minis(?) ꝫꝰ(?) ...     ["Tenrab;/Termab;" could be "terminis/terminab(us)"; uncertain]
image-002 l.11: sic p(ro)p(?)o(?) . ꝗ(?) . e(?) [..]r(?) sic ti(?) m(aio)r(?) ꝫꝫ(?) ꝓ(?) . ꝗ(?) . a(?)...     [the line runs into the curl]
(Lines 9-11 continue into the curl at right with fragments "ꝗ(?)e mīa / ꝯ ꝫꝫ / ꝗ(?) a ꝯ" that I can't read reliably.)

(B) Sideways cursive layer, read from image-001 rotated 90 degrees clockwise (line numbers in reading order of the rotated view, from the top of the visible area; read from the reduced overview, not a native tile)
B l.1: ...[..]ranib(us)(?) ex(?)[..]cationib(us)(?) ac [..]rac(?)...
B l.2: ...[..]ue(?)ex(?)[..] . ac in d(?)ystrictib(us)(?)     [could be "districtibus"]
B l.3: Q(?)uib(us)(?)/Duob(us)(?) tam(en)(?)[..]ꝰ in [..]
B l.4: Sacerdotib(us) . iustia(?)/c(?)ustria(?) a p(ro)[..]
B l.5: ...mo(?)ꝰ a parentib(us) . r(?)eu(?)i[..]ā(?) a [..]
B l.6: + doctorib(us) . studiu(m) a ...
B l.7: ...ꝰ(?) . fidelitas a mil(itibus)(?)...
B l.8: ...gr(?)andia(?)/[..]rancia(?) a ciuib(us)(?) .
B l.9: ...[..]ins(?)/ius(?) a diuitib(us) . p[..]
B l.10: ...dus(?)ꝰ . p(ro)dic(?)ia(?)/prudencia(?)     [uncertain]
B l.11: ...[..]cundia(?)/[..]undiā(?) segni(?)u(?)[..]     [could be "verecundia" or "-cundia" followed by "seguin-/segnu-"; uncertain]
Visible above B l.1 near the left edge (image-001 top-left, sideways): "...[..]ib(us) . ꝛ s(?)c(?)e(?)" — this is the end of an earlier line, partly under the plastic strip.

(C) Scribbles at the upper right of image-001: loops and "E(?)go(?)" / "Ego(?)" flourishes, perhaps pen trials. Not transcribed.

LIMITATIONS
- (A) is a curled, torn corner piece, so its lines are cut at the left and bottom and disappear into the curl at right. The abbreviation system is dense, and most of my readings are uncertain letter-by-letter values, not secure words.
- (B) was read only from the reduced overview, and the curled piece and the label frame cover part of it.
- Suggested next step: a native-resolution tile of the sideways cursive layer (B), especially below and left of the curl. If conservation allows, flatten or photograph the curl so the right ends of (A)'s lines can be seen. Imaging the verso of piece (A) would also help.
